discovery: Circuit quantum electrodynamics: strong coupling of superconducting qubits to microwave photons
motivation: The 2025 Prize recognized macroscopic quantum effects in Josephson circuits. Circuit quantum electrodynamics is what turned those effects into a controllable quantum technology. In 2004 Blais and co-workers proposed coupling a superconducting qubit to an on-chip microwave resonator. That same year Wallraff, Schoelkopf and colleagues at Yale demonstrated strong coupling between a single artificial atom and a single photon, reaching regimes that atomic cavity QED could hardly access. The architecture made high-fidelity dispersive qubit readout, photon-mediated two-qubit gates, bosonic encodings and microwave quantum optics possible. Today it underpins every major superconducting processor, including recent demonstrations of error correction below threshold. Circuit QED is also a new laboratory for light–matter interaction in its own right, including the ultrastrong-coupling regime and the generation and detection of single microwave photons.
